original_question: If two finitely presented abelian lattice-ordered groups satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences, must those two groups be isomorphic?
target_in_paper: Section 1.1, Problem 1.55* (D. Mundici): "If finitely presented abelian ℓ-groups satisfy the same first order sentences, must they be isomorphic?" ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended problem very closely: it keeps the crucial restrictions "finitely presented" and "abelian," uses first-order indistinguishability as the hypothesis, and asks for isomorphism as the conclusion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
missing_details: State explicitly that the structures are abelian ℓ-groups, i.e. lattice-ordered abelian groups; this is the paper’s standard terminology. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Specify that "satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences" means elementary equivalence in the first-order language of ℓ-groups, not merely in the pure group language; the paper’s comment explicitly refers to the countable language of ℓ-groups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Clarify that "finitely presented" is meant in the ℓ-group sense, i.e. with respect to the group and lattice operations, not merely as an abstract abelian group. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

Clarify that "isomorphic" means ℓ-isomorphic, preserving both the abelian group structure and the lattice order; that is the ambient notion of isomorphism throughout Section 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
refined_question: Let G and H be finitely presented abelian ℓ-groups (that is, lattice-ordered abelian groups), finitely presented in the ℓ-group language {+, −, 0, ∨, ∧}. If G and H are elementarily equivalent in that first-order language, must G and H be ℓ-isomorphic?
justification: The draft is essentially Problem 1.55* almost verbatim, so only the ambient language and the intended notion of isomorphism needed to be made explicit. The nearby comment on Problem 1.55 shows why the scope should remain exactly as stated in the paper: there is a positive result when the number of generators is at most 3, but the analogous statement is false if one weakens "finitely presented" to "finitely generated," via the family D(ξ)=Z⊕Zξ of dense totally ordered abelian ℓ-groups inside R. This confirms that your draft is targeting Problem 1.55* rather than the broader neighboring Problem 1.54 or any finitely generated variant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
